extracted.intended_audience: General public, stakeholders in South African environmental management (citizens, NGOs, industry, permit applicants, researchers)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment's legal mandate, legislative/regulatory framework, strategic vision/mission/values, core interventions, and public contact/notice channels in South Africa. Primarily informational for stakeholders engaging with departmental processes, legislation, permits, or public participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal mandate and core business
rubrics_metrics.description: The legal mandate and core business of the Department of Forestry, Fisheries and the Environment (DFFE) are to manage, protect and conserve South Africa’s environment and natural resources. The mandate is informed by section 24 of the Constitution of the Republic of South Africa, 1996 which affords everyone the right to (a) an environment that is not harmful to their health or well-being; and (b) to have the environment protected for the benefit of present and future generations, through reasonable legislative and other measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary statutory standard justifying departmental action and policy: policies, regulations, permits and interventions should be designed to realize section 24 rights and to manage/protect/conserve natural resources for current and future generations. Use this constitutional framing when assessing legitimacy of DFFE measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental management legislative/regulatory framework
rubrics_metrics.description: To give effect to this constitutional environmental right and the need for sound environmental management and sustainable development, the DFFE has ... developed a comprehensive environmental management legislative/regulatory framework. This regulatory framework comprises acts of parliament (environmental laws), regulations, policies, norms and standards, and other regulatory tools aimed at promoting sound environmental management practices in order to protect and conserve the environment for the benefit of current and future generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating or producing regulatory measures or guidance, ensure they fit into one of the listed instrument types (acts, regulations, policies, norms and standards, other tools) and are aimed at promoting sound environmental management and sustainable development. The framework indicates the legal/administrative channels through which environmental protection is to be implemented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critical environmental management interventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical environmental management interventions by the DFFE include raising awareness on key environment issues and promoting a culture of environmental activism among ordinary citizens, building capacity within the sector, and establishing and strengthening national, regional and global partnerships to address common environmental challenges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These interventions represent priority approaches the department expects to use alongside regulatory tools: public awareness/activism, capacity building, and partnerships. Proposed programs, public comments, or project designs should address or align with one or more of these intervention types where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vision (strategic aim)
rubrics_metrics.description: Vision: A prosperous, equitable and resilient society living in harmony with our natural resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the high-level aspirational criterion against which long-term plans and strategies should be assessed: do proposed policies or projects advance prosperity, equity, resilience, and harmony with natural resources?

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission (strategic role)
rubrics_metrics.description: Mission: Providing leadership in environmental management, conservation and protection towards a sustainable development and a climate resilient South Africa, for the benefit of all South Africans and the global community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this mission statement to evaluate whether departmental actions provide leadership in environmental management, contribute to conservation/protection, support sustainable development, and build climate resilience domestically and in cooperation internationally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Values (service and conduct standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Values: Passion: driven by a deep commitment to environmental stewardship. Proactive and innovative: embracing forward - thinking and solution - driven approaches. People-centric: prioritising services to communities, stakeholders, and internal relations with respect and empathy. Integrity: upholding transparency, honesty and accountability in all actions. Performance-driven: focused on delivering impactful, efficient, and high - quality services. Inclusivity: empowering all South African citizens through public participation and ensuring transformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These value statements function as behavioural and service-quality criteria for departmental staff and programs. Policies, public engagement processes, and communications should reflect passion for stewardship, proactive/innovative approaches, people-centred service, integrity/transparency, performance orientation, and inclusivity (including public participation and transformation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislative and public-instrument channels (transparency and participation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Site navigation lists: Legislation, Bills, Green papers, White papers, Acts and regulations, International agreements and obligations, Gazetted notices, Appeals. These are the instruments and channels through which lawmaking, consultation and public notices are published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For notice-and-comment and public participation processes, consult the indicated instruments (green/white papers, gazetted notices, bills) and use the listed channels to find consultation opportunities. The presence of these categories implies formal avenues for notices, publication of proposed measures, and appeals processes that stakeholders should monitor and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact, operating hours and reporting channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Operating hours: Monday - Friday: 08:00 - 16:30. Contact numbers and emails: switchboard +27 12 399 9000; DFFE call centre +27 86 111 2468 | callcentre@dffe.gov.za; Environmental crimes hotline 0800 205 005 | envirocrime@dffe.gov.za; fisheries/FRAP enquiries and recreational fishing enquiries with phone numbers and emails listed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical procedural requirement: stakeholders and members of the public should use these contact points and observe operating hours for enquiries, reporting environmental crimes, fisheries-related matters, or to seek information about notices and participation processes. Include these contacts in outreach or submissions where appropriate.
